sections.churn_summary: Hold-buffer guards are live on all three focus tracks (`exit_confirm_screens=2`, `reentry_cooldown_screens=1`, `min_rebalance_notional_gbp=10.0`), and recent operational noise is low: every track shows `buffered_holdings=0`, empty `exit_streak` / `reentry_cooldown`, `duplicate_day_skip=false`, and `adjacent_flip_count=0` over the 7-day window. That said, lifetime cost drag remains elevated on the control and primary books — `rules` at 30.5% (`cost_drag=0.3051`, `trade_count=51`) and `ai_judgment` at 23.0% (`cost_drag=0.2298`, `trade_count=34`) — while `momentum_grace` sits at 2.9% on only 5 lifetime trades. The 7-day buffered-hold replay suggests `exit_confirm_screens=2` is doing useful work on `rules` (2 fewer trades, 4.3pp lower simulated cost drag vs screens=1), but on `ai_judgment` the screen-count delta is negligible (`trade_count_delta=-1`, `cost_drag_delta=-0.0007`). The single biggest operational learning gap is epoch readiness on the primary track: `ai_judgment` restarted its knob epoch on 2026-08-26 with `post_apply_trade_count=0`, `equity_marks=1`, and `benchmark_span_available=false`, so guard effectiveness cannot yet be judged on the book that actually drives learning decisions.

sections.proposed_experiments:
1. [paper_churn] Rules track `min_rebalance_notional_gbp` ladder replay (10 → 25 → 50 GBP) on the same 7-day rebalance log — expected learning value: quantify whether sub-£25 trims (3 trades in `trades_last_7d` including 1 trim) drive a material share of the 30.5% lifetime cost drag without changing `exit_confirm_screens=2`.

2. [paper_churn] Add `momentum_grace` to the buffered-hold counterfactual panel with `exit_confirm_screens` 1 vs 2 replay — expected learning value: close the replay gap vs `rules`/`ai_judgment` and test whether momentum grace plus a 1-screen exit path changes trade count or cost drag given `trades_last_7d.total=0` but lifetime `trade_count=5`.

3. [offline_sim] Archive-lab full-history replay for `rules` and `ai_judgment` pre-2026-08-24 log window — expected learning value: validate whether the 7-day counterfactual (where screens=1 adds +4.3pp cost drag on rules but is flat on ai_judgment) holds over the full 51/34-trade lifetimes cited in payload limitations.
